paragraphs.source_en: People who appear carefree on the surface, if one taps the bottom of their hearts, give off somewhere a melancholy sound. Even Mr. Dokusen, who seems to have attained perfect enlightenment, still plants both feet on the ground. Mr. Meitei may be lighthearted enough, but his world is not the beautiful world one sees in a painting. Mr. Kangetsu has stopped polishing glass balls and has finally brought his wife from his native place; that is proper enough, but if such propriety continues too long, he will surely grow bored. In another ten years or so, Mr. Tofu too will surely realize the folly of recklessly dedicating new-style poems to women. As for Mr. Tatara, whether he is a creature of the water or of the mountains is rather hard to determine; if he can spend his whole life proudly treating people to champagne, that will be splendid enough. Fuji of the Suzuki household will go on rolling forever. If one rolls, mud sticks to one; yet even covered in mud, one has more standing than those who cannot roll. Born a cat and dwelling in the world of men, I have already passed more than two years here. I used to think to myself, “Surely there can hardly be another cat of such excellent discernment as I.” Yet the other day, a fellow cat unknown to me, named Murr, suddenly made a great stir, which rather astonished me. On inquiring carefully, I learned that in fact he had died a hundred years ago. It seems that, out of some casual curiosity, he deliberately became a ghost and came on business from the distant land of the dead in order to frighten me. When this cat set out to meet his mother, he carried a fish in his mouth as a token of greeting, but along the way he could no longer restrain himself and ate it. Being just such an unfilial cat, he was said to possess wit that by no means lost to a human being’s, and at times even composed poems that astonished his master. If such a hero had already appeared a century ago, then a worthless cat like me ought long since to have asked leave and retired to that tranquil land of nonaction.

units.source_en: People who appear carefree on the surface, if one taps the bottom of their hearts, give off somewhere a melancholy sound.
units.source_zh: 表面看去，这些人似乎都是对一切事物无所谓的人，但如果叩开他们的心扉，就会发出某种悲凉的声音。

units.source_en: Even Mr. Dokusen, who seems to have attained perfect enlightenment, still plants both feet on the ground.
units.source_zh: 似乎一切都大彻大悟了的独仙君，其实他的两条腿仍然踩在地面上；

units.source_en: Mr. Meitei may be lighthearted enough, but his world is not the beautiful world one sees in a painting.
units.source_zh: 迷亭君也许是无忧无虑的吧，但是他的世界也不是画中那般优美的世界；

units.source_en: Mr. Kangetsu has stopped polishing glass balls and has finally brought his wife from his native place; that is proper enough, but if such propriety continues too long, he will surely grow bored.

ja.t: りをやめてとうとうお

units.source_zh: 寒月君不再磨玻璃球了，他从故乡把妻子接来，这倒是稳妥的，但这种生活长期继续下去，他会感到倦怠的；

units.source_en: In another ten years or so, Mr. Tofu too will surely realize the folly of recklessly dedicating new-style poems to women.
units.source_zh: 东风君再过上十年八年，总会省悟到一味作新体诗去献给女人的是非吧；

units.source_en: As for Mr. Tatara, whether he is a creature of the water or of the mountains is rather hard to determine; if he can spend his whole life proudly treating people to champagne, that will be splendid enough.
units.source_zh: 多多良君是能成精呢还是能作怪，这就很难说，如果他能够做到一辈子都得意地请人喝香槟酒，那就再好不过啦；

units.source_en: Fuji of the Suzuki household will go on rolling forever. If one rolls, mud sticks to one; yet even covered in mud, one has more standing than those who cannot roll.
units.source_zh: 铃木家的阿藤还会不停地滚下去的，滚，就要沾一身泥巴，即使沾得满身污泥，总要比不滚的人吃得开；

units.source_en: Born a cat and dwelling in the world of men, I have already passed more than two years here.
units.source_zh: 我生为一只猫儿，住在这人世上，转瞬已过了两个年头。

units.source_en: I used to think to myself, “Surely there can hardly be another cat of such excellent discernment as I.”
units.source_zh: 我常想：“像我这样卓越的有见识者恐怕是难得再有吧。”

units.source_en: Yet the other day, a fellow cat unknown to me, named Murr, suddenly made a great stir, which rather astonished me.
units.source_zh: 想不到就在前一阵子，出现了一个与我从未谋过面、名叫“摩尔”的同族，它在那里大出风头，使我着实吃了一惊。

units.source_en: On inquiring carefully, I learned that in fact he had died a hundred years ago.
units.source_zh: 我仔细一打听，原来它于一百年以前就死去。

units.source_en: It seems that, out of some casual curiosity, he deliberately became a ghost and came on business from the distant land of the dead in order to frighten me.
units.source_zh: 不过，据说可能是出于一时的好奇心，所以有意变成幽灵，从辽远的幽冥界出差到这里来，以便惊吓我。

units.source_en: When this cat set out to meet his mother, he carried a fish in his mouth as a token of greeting, but along the way he could no longer restrain himself and ate it.
units.source_zh: 这只猫儿去和它的母亲会面时叼了一尾鱼作为礼物前往，结果在半路上馋得忍无可忍，便将鱼吃了。

units.source_en: Being just such an unfilial cat, he was said to possess wit that by no means lost to a human being’s, and at times even composed poems that astonished his master.
units.source_zh: 正因为它是个这样不孝的猫儿，所以它的才气不比人差，据说有时候它还做诗来使它的主人吃惊哩。

units.source_en: If such a hero had already appeared a century ago, then a worthless cat like me ought long since to have asked leave and retired to that tranquil land of nonaction.

ja.t: してもいいはずであった。

units.source_zh: 像这样俊杰之物，已经出现在一个世纪之前，那么像我这样不成材的猫儿，早就应该告个假，回到那清静无为乡去啦。

paragraphs.source_zh: 表面看去，这些人似乎都是对一切事物无所谓的人，但如果叩开他们的心扉，就会发出某种悲凉的声音。似乎一切都大彻大悟了的独仙君，其实他的两条腿仍然踩在地面上；迷亭君也许是无忧无虑的吧，但是他的世界也不是画中那般优美的世界；寒月君不再磨玻璃球了，他从故乡把妻子接来，这倒是稳妥的，但这种生活长期继续下去，他会感到倦怠的；东风君再过上十年八年，总会省悟到一味作新体诗去献给女人的是非吧；多多良君是能成精呢还是能作怪，这就很难说，如果他能够做到一辈子都得意地请人喝香槟酒，那就再好不过啦；铃木家的阿藤还会不停地滚下去的，滚，就要沾一身泥巴，即使沾得满身污泥，总要比不滚的人吃得开；我生为一只猫儿，住在这人世上，转瞬已过了两个年头。我常想：“像我这样卓越的有见识者恐怕是难得再有吧。”想不到就在前一阵子，出现了一个与我从未谋过面、名叫“摩尔”的同族，它在那里大出风头，使我着实吃了一惊。我仔细一打听，原来它于一百年以前就死去。不过，据说可能是出于一时的好奇心，所以有意变成幽灵，从辽远的幽冥界出差到这里来，以便惊吓我。这只猫儿去和它的母亲会面时叼了一尾鱼作为礼物前往，结果在半路上馋得忍无可忍，便将鱼吃了。正因为它是个这样不孝的猫儿，所以它的才气不比人差，据说有时候它还做诗来使它的主人吃惊哩。像这样俊杰之物，已经出现在一个世纪之前，那么像我这样不成材的猫儿，早就应该告个假，回到那清静无为乡去啦。

paragraphs.source_en: Sooner or later, my master will die. Old Kaneda, burdened by greed, is already a living corpse. The autumn leaves have for the most part already fallen. If death is the inescapable destiny of all things, and being alive is not of much use, then dying early may be the wiser course. According to what the gentlemen were saying just now, the fate of human beings ultimately comes down to suicide. If one is even a little careless, a cat too may be forced to be born into this world where everything is constrained and uncomfortable. A terrifying thought indeed. For some reason, I too began to feel low in spirits. I shall drink some of the beer Mr. Tatara brought, and cheer myself up a little.

units.source_en: Sooner or later, my master will die.
units.source_zh: 主人迟早要死的。

units.source_en: Old Kaneda, burdened by greed, is already a living corpse.
units.source_zh: 金田那老头儿受欲心所累，早已成了活死人。

units.source_en: The autumn leaves have for the most part already fallen.
units.source_zh: 秋天的树叶已经大体上落光。

units.source_en: If death is the inescapable destiny of all things, and being alive is not of much use, then dying early may be the wiser course.
units.source_zh: 死是万物难以逃脱的宿命，如果活着也不见得有什么用处，不如早些死了更聪明些。

units.source_en: According to what the gentlemen were saying just now, the fate of human beings ultimately comes down to suicide.
units.source_zh: 根据刚才各位先生的说法，人的命运最后归结为自杀。

units.source_en: If one is even a little careless, a cat too may be forced to be born into this world where everything is constrained and uncomfortable.

ja.t: れなくてはならなくなる。

units.source_zh: 如果稍微麻痹大意，那么猫儿也不得不生于这万事不自在的人世上。

units.source_en: A terrifying thought indeed.
units.source_zh: 真是可怕呀。

units.source_en: For some reason, I too began to feel low in spirits.
units.source_zh: 不知为什么，我心里也不痛快起来了。

units.source_en: I shall drink some of the beer Mr. Tatara brought, and cheer myself up a little.
units.source_zh: 我也去喝点多多良君带来的啤酒，打起精神来高兴高兴吧。

paragraphs.source_zh: 主人迟早要死的。金田那老头儿受欲心所累，早已成了活死人。秋天的树叶已经大体上落光。死是万物难以逃脱的宿命，如果活着也不见得有什么用处，不如早些死了更聪明些。根据刚才各位先生的说法，人的命运最后归结为自杀。如果稍微麻痹大意，那么猫儿也不得不生于这万事不自在的人世上。真是可怕呀。不知为什么，我心里也不痛快起来了。我也去喝点多多良君带来的啤酒，打起精神来高兴高兴吧。
